text:
Martin Lewis has revealed all the financial benefits of marrying in a Valentine’s Special of its ITV program.
The founder of British experts who saves money, 52, marked the February 14 holidays by explaining why tie the knot was “financially valuable”, and how to take advantage of the eight bonuses.
Speaking at the Martin Lewis Money Show live on Thursday night, the financial expert revealed how all benefits only apply to married couples or in civil associations, and not to those who are only living together.
The host said: “None of these apply if they only live together, I don’t care if they have lived together for 20 years, it makes no difference, I don’t care if you have children, it makes no difference. It’s about marriage and civil associations .
However, Martin warned that he was discussing the potential benefits of marriage between two people who trust each other, and not talking about weddings, which he warned “can be very expensive.”
‘They don’t need to be. They do not borrow their pleasant and clean marriage without him, ‘he urged the spectators.
Explaining that the benefits begin from the day a couple marries, Martin explained that the first advantage was an exemption of marriage taxes or civil society of £ 1,260.
“So this is what is called the matrimonial fiscal assignment, and it works whenever one of you has aging of around 90,” said the financial expert. “Specifically, one of you needs to have been born after the fifth of April 1935.

‘It is fine, then the non -taxpayer can request Gov.UK to transfer 10 percent of its tax free allocation to the basic rate taxpayer.
‘The net result of that is that the non -taxpayer now has an assignment of £ 11,310, and the taxpayer has a combined allocation of £ 13,830.
“Now that 10 percent of the additional tax free allocation they have, remember, they would have paid taxes on 20 percent, so the profit there is £ 252 per year, and that is why they move through the works “.
Martin warned: “You must do this quickly, because this year, it is every fiscal year, and the fiscal year ends on April 5. It can claim up to four fiscal years as long as it is eligible, which means a total gain of £ 1,258.
